clue.text: Last part of race maybe sorted out

definitions.meaning: the home stretch of a racecourse, the run-in, is one example
put right, settled, as when matters are set in order

explanation.surface: A commentator remarks that the final leg of a race has perhaps been arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stretch of a racetrack carries this name, and a thing put in order has been made so.

clue.text: Breakaway group declined to let Conservative in

indicators.note: to let something in is to admit it, so one piece is placed within the other
completes the phrase 'let ... in', saying the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: the sun declined, or set, sinking low

explanation.surface: A splinter faction refused to admit a Tory into its ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter faction that has broken from a larger religious body is called by this word.

clue.text: Offensive superiors may pull it

definitions.meaning: foul-smelling, rancid, as in a nasty stench
a senior who pulls this uses status to get their way

explanation.surface: In a military attack, higher officers might exert their seniority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like a noun, a military push; it is the adjective meaning foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means foul or smelly; to 'pull' it is to use one's seniority, an idiom.

clue.text: What was gathered at the wicket about to penetrate boundary?

parts.note: a cricket batsman at the wicket is in, currently batting

indicators.note: one piece pierces into the middle of the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a fence marks the boundary of a field
RE is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what was caught at the wicket, about to cross the boundary rope?
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' suggests a catch at cricket, but here means concluded. 'at the wicket' is cricket's word for currently batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one has gathered is a conclusion reached by reasoning, a deduction.

clue.text: Both comrades at sea out of action

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pair of sailor comrades on a voyage are both injured and unable to serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for a soldier disabled and unable to fight.

clue.text: Epicurean opponent hosting current party in recession

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: an opponent is a foe

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the word for party is read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A gourmet adversary throws a party despite an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is devoted to fine eating, which is what a gastronome enthusiast is.

clue.text: Rider cryptically having the advantage

definitions.meaning: a rider is a single person up on a horse, read cryptically as the answer
being a step ahead of a rival

explanation.definitionFit: Being a step ahead, holding a lead over a rival, is the idiom; a horseman is literally one person mounted.

clue.text: Hopeless days in Rome, one having left partnership

indicators.note: the numeral has departed from the Latin word, so it is taken out

parts.note: dies is Latin for day or days
I is the Roman numeral one
a pairing is a partnership

explanation.surface: Someone gives up hope during a Roman holiday after a companion walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' signals Latin: dies means day. Removing I leaves DES.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling without hope is to be in a state of despair, so the two adjectives match.

clue.text: Difficult to shift, as were troops on the Somme

definitions.text: as were troops on the Somme
definitions.meaning: First World War soldiers at the Somme fought from dug-in trenches

explanation.definitionFit: Firmly rooted habits or views are dug in, and soldiers of the 1916 Somme battle literally dug in.

clue.text: Latest of restrictions in force affected trees

indicators.note: to be affected is to be altered or put on, so these letters are rearranged
the latest item is the final one, so take the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: New rules now in force have harmed the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' anagrams IN FORCE to CONIFER; the S comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Pines, firs and spruces are cone-bearing evergreens, examples of this kind of tree.

clue.text: County with the very thing in accommodation

parts.note: BEDS is short for Bedfordshire, an English county
'it' means just the thing, the ideal, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A county comes with exactly what is needed when it comes to housing.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is short for Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat for sleeping and living in, a common British form of rented lodging.

clue.text: Breed of dog on street, unusually bearing right?

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the jumbled letters hold the abbreviation within
done in an unusual way, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A curious sight: some breed of dog walking down the street, oddly keeping to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breed of dog' wants to be the definition; only 'Breed' is, and 'dog' joins the anagram. 'unusually' rearranges DOG ON STREET; 'bearing' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-tan Scottish gundog, it is one specific breed of dog.

clue.text: Supremacy accorded local lions?

definitions.meaning: the top position, the most honoured spot
a group of lions is a pride, and local ones are a pride belonging to the place

explanation.definitionFit: The most prominent or honoured position is the idiom; read literally, a band of big cats from a given location.

clue.text: Badly shod curate flopped spectacularly

indicators.note: badly done means messed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A clergyman wearing ill-fitting shoes tripped and fell flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail dramatically, often to be knocked out of a competition, is the idiom.

clue.text: Badgers bring in new disease, ultimately infecting us

parts.note: to import goods is to bring them in

indicators.note: an infection gets inside its host, so these letters go into the pronoun

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wild badgers carry a fresh illness that ends up spreading to people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' looks like the animals; it is a verb meaning pesters.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently with requests, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: The writer contributing to series that could be tripe

indicators.note: the author's pronoun is put into the middle of the series word

parts.note: a run is a series, like a winning run
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An author writes for a TV series that might turn out to be rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' suggests nonsense, but means the edible stomach lining.
explanation.definitionFit: The first stomach of a cow or sheep, which as food is sold as tripe.

clue.text: Haggard villain I caught crossing state

indicators.note: the outer letters stretch across the word for state, holding it within

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to aver is to state or assert

explanation.surface: A careworn scoundrel says he was arrested while crossing the border of a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpse-like, deathly pale and gaunt, which is how a worn and drawn face looks.

clue.text: Animated, like a thug casing V&A?

indicators.note: a thug casing a joint surrounds it, so the museum's letters go within

parts.note: a thug is vicious, brutally violent
the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, its letters V and A

explanation.surface: Lively, like a ruffian checking out the London museum before a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'case' a place is criminal slang for scouting it before a robbery. The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and spirited in manner, full of animation, a close synonym.

clue.text: Official staff previously rung several times

indicators.note: the other piece comes before, earlier in the word

parts.note: a rung of a ladder or chair is a spoke, so several are spokes
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: An officer recalls the bell having been rung repeatedly earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rung' looks like the bell verb; it is a noun, a ladder's crosspiece.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who speaks for an organisation is its representative mouthpiece.

clue.text: Where we meet goddess, making final 90 degree turn

indicators.note: on a compass, turning the last letter, south, a quarter turn gives east

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love

explanation.surface: We arrange to meet a goddess, then take one last right-angle turn to get there.
explanation.walkthrough: S and E are compass points: a quarter turn from south reaches east.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where an event or gathering is held is its meeting-place.

clue.text: Deplorable teenage acts finally destroy business

indicators.note: deplorable acts are wretched, so these letters are wrecked and rearranged
finally means at the end, so take the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Awful antics by teenagers end up ruining a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm handling the buying and selling of houses is a kind of business.

clue.text: Some particular premises unfinished

indicators.note: an unfinished word lacks its ending, so the final letter goes

parts.note: theses are propositions put forward, premises of an argument

explanation.surface: A detail: certain properties are left half-built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premises' looks like buildings, but means propositions. Dropping the last S leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a determiner, it points to certain specified items, a particular few.

clue.text: S American coin cashier's taken in

indicators.note: the letters are held within these words, enclosed by them

explanation.surface: A South American coin has been taken by the cashier.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Andean people of Peru, so a native South American.

clue.text: Build up healthily, filling out with exercise

indicators.note: with the filling removed, only the outer letters remain

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Bulk up healthily, getting bigger with workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling out' looks like gaining weight; it means emptying the word of its filling.
explanation.definitionFit: To build up a product is to promote it with extravagant publicity.

clue.text: Cats — over fifty disposed of by relatives

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the numeral is got rid of by the relatives word, so it is removed

parts.note: uncles are relatives
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Some cats, over fifty, are got rid of by family members.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also known by this name, so these are wild felines.

clue.text: Lawman from area still going round collecting rent

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the second piece is placed inside
turning round means reading the word for still backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
rent is the past tense of rend, so torn

explanation.surface: A lawman from the district is still making his rounds collecting rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money owed; it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer, especially in the US, who acts for clients in legal matters.

clue.text: Decoration from Territorial Army without backing

parts.note: TA is the abbreviation for the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for without is read in reverse

parts.note: less means without, as in 'less sugar'

explanation.surface: Reservists award a medal to someone with no support.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging tuft of threads is an ornament on cushions, curtains or a mortarboard.

clue.text: Disciplined horse moves a long time after groom

indicators.note: the second piece comes after, later in the word

parts.note: to groom someone is to dress them, make them neat
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A horse performs trained steps a good while after being groomed.
explanation.definitionFit: This equestrian sport displays a horse's trained, controlled movements.
